## Problem

The current workflow isn't scaling well; it's too slow to handle 
autochamber LI-8100/7810 data.

## High level changes 

The `bbl-tweaks` branch has many changes, but at a high level,
they are, in descending (imho) order of importance,

* Separate functionality
* Do as much prep work as possible _before_ the user-time-intensive steps
* Do work only once; save incremental progress
* Keep data in data files and code in code files
* Use higher-performance tools, formats, etc.

## Separate functionality & prep work

The first script is `1-Download_Extract_Metadata.Rmd`:

* Downloads _all_ 8100 and 7810 files
* Splits the large 7810 files into per-day files (LI7810_20240613.parquet, LI7810_20240614.parquet, etc.)
* Splits the 8100 files into individual observations and compiles extracted metadata into a single file
* Runs some basic diagnostics

## Separate functionality & prep work

The second script is `2-Clock_Offsets.R`:

* Reads the metadata prepared by script 1
* Reads the day-specific 7810 data file
* For each plot, compute optimal clock offset for best fit between metadata (8100) times and measurement (7810) times based on linear trends of CO2
* Allows the user to accept/reject this and substitute their own value
* Allows the user to provide collar-specific offsets if needed

## Do work only once

Skip already-downloaded files

```
if(file.exists(outfile)) {

	message("\tskipped existing file ")
	
} else {

	message("\tdownloading...")

# (proceed to download the file...)
```

## Do work only once

Don't do work we've already done

```
for(f in file.list.7810) {

    # Check whether we've already split this file; 
    # name and hash both have to match
    
    dig <- digest::digest(file = file.path(RAW_DIR, f))
    
    if(nrow(filter(already_split, file == f, hash == dig)) == 1) {
        message(f, " has already been split; skipping")
        next
    }

# (proceed to split the file...)
```

## Do work only once

Don't do work we've already done

```
# (after we've split the file...)

# Record that we have split this file

message("\tUpdating ", ALREADY_SPLIT_LIST)

already_split |> 
	# remove any older entries for this file
	filter(!file == f) |> 
	
	# ...and add a new one
	bind_rows(tibble(file = f, hash = dig, date = Sys.Date())) ->
	already_split
	
write_csv(already_split, file = ALREADY_SPLIT_LIST)
```

## Do work only once

Save work as we go

```
# How many result rows are already in the processed table?
# If identical to numbers of observations to process, assume
# that we already have done this file and move on

n_processed <- length(grep(f_no_extension, processed$obs, fixed = TRUE))

if(n_processed == n_obs) {
	message("\t", n_processed, " observations already processed; moving on") 
	next
	
} else {
	# remove any old data for this file (in case it was previously
	# partially processed, for example)
	processed <- filter(processed, !grepl(f_no_extension, obs, fixed = TRUE))
	
}
```

## Keep data in data files and code in code files

I'm not a fan of code being customized to modify metadata, resulting
in a separate code file for each day/run/whatever, but it works
for _small_ data.

For large data, that way madness lies. Again imho.

## Use higher-performance tools

These include

* [Apache Parquet files](https://parquet.apache.org) for the large 7810 data and 8100 metadata files
* Caches (effectively what many of those intermediate files are)
* `readr::read_csv()` instead of base R's `read.csv()`
* Don't write unnecessary files (e.g. the `txt` single-observation files); just process them immmediately

## Quick start guide

### Step 1

The first script can be run by rendering `1-Download_Extract_Metadata.Rmd`. 
It will take a while when run for the first time! But you can
stop it anytime and it will more or less pick up where it left
off when re-run.

Note that I have committed `SoilFluxes_8100_Metadata_processed_final.parquet`
to the repository (in `Processed_Data/`) -- this, along with the single-day 7810 files, is the major and time-consuming 
output of script 1.

## Quick start guide

### Step 2

The second script is a plain `.R` file and is _interactive_
(it will ask the user questions). When you have the single-day
LI7810 files ready, it can be used. 

However, I have committed
one of these single-day files to the repo, `LI7810_20240608.parquet`,
allowing script 2 to be tried out immmediately.
